sources.note: No Esuma/Essouma entry at all (a full-text search for stress/accent over both scanned copies). By 1903 Delafosse describes the native population of Assinie (Mafya, Komando, France) as 'Asini ou Asoko' Agni speakers mixed with Apolloniens (Zema) and Mekyibo, 'leur dialecte, surtout à Assinie, a fortement subi l'influence du zéma' (pp. 106-107) — i.e. the Esuma language was already gone; confirms 'undocumented'.

Nothing; Esuma, individual, extinct; references Ethnologue/Glottolog/Wikipedia only.

sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Verbatim: 'Esuma (Essouma) is an extinct undocumented language of uncertain classification within the Kwa branch.. once spoken in the villages of Assinie (Asini) and Mafia.. The Esuma were vassals of the Sanwi capital Krinjabo, and shifted to the Anyin and Nzima languages.' Infobox: 'Extinct ca. 1800'. Cites only MultiTree, Glottolog, and the 1971 Abidjan congress proceedings.
Nothing; only 'An Esuma language, extinct ca. 1800, remains unclassified.'
